newsitem.title: USA: Top aide says Mideast peace not ripe for Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Top aide says Mideast peace not ripe for Clinton.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's national security adviser on Sunday brushed off a Palestinian call for Clinton to make a dramatic intervention in the Middle East peace process.

"Presidential involvement is happening every day," security adviser Samuel Berger said in an interview on CNN. He said the time was not ripe for a Camp David-style summit like that staged by President Jimmy Carter in 1978 to forge a peace between Israel and Egypt.

"The point here is not dramatic moments, the point here is progress in the peace process," Berger said. "And the parties themselves have to be prepared to make the kinds of compromises, the kinds of commitments, that would make a dramatic moment not only dramatic but successful."

Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat sent Clinton a letter on Friday declaring U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross's latest mission a failure and asking Clinton to interve personally in deadlocked Israeli-Palestinian talks.
Berger said the United States would continue to push to get the dialogue back on track, adding, however: "You don't have grand gestures unless you believe they're going to be successful."
